sentences.text: Through this part, higher capital gains lower a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) slowly at first, then faster, from about 60% at 0 US dollars to about 6% at 6849 US dollars, flattening out near the bottom because the predicted chance cannot go much lower.
Higher capital losses lower it steadily, from about 60% at 0 to about 28% at 1887 US dollars.

This part combines marital status and relationship in the household: being never married rather than married raises a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) from about 60% to about 98%, being separated to about 96% and being a child of the household rather than a husband to about 89%, while being a wife lowers it to about 16%.

Being born in India raises it more for husbands: from about 60% to about 92% for a husband, against about 42% to about 76% for people whose relationship in the household is other than husband, other relative, own child or wife.
Through it, never having worked raises it to above 99% (the model has little data on this, n = 9), and being married to a member of the armed forces lowers it to about 52%.

This part adds up the person's background: being a woman raises a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) from about 60% to about 85%, and older age lowers it steadily, from about 73% at 22 to about 41% at 58 years.

Being born in the outlying US territories (Guam, US Virgin Islands) or Colombia raises it to above 99%, in Laos to about 93% (the model has little data on this, n = 17), in Vietnam to about 87% and in Thailand or China to about 84%, while being born in Italy lowers it to about 45% and in England to about 48%.
Being Asian or Pacific Islander rather than White lowers it to about 51%, and a race other than Asian or Pacific Islander, White or 'other' raises it to about 68%.
A higher census sampling weight lowers it slowly at first, then faster, from about 62% at 66,572 to about 56% at 328,216.

This part adds up the person's work: compared with a professional job, other service work raises a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) to about 92%, farming or fishing and a missing occupation to about 88%, handling or cleaning to about 82% and machine operating or inspecting to about 75%.
Longer working hours lower it steadily, from about 73% at 24 to about 47% at 55 hours a week.

Being self-employed (not incorporated) raises it to about 77% and working for a state government to about 68%, while an executive or managerial job lowers it to about 53% and working for the federal government to about 48%.

This part adds up the person's education: a higher education level lowers a typical person's predicted chance of a low income ($50,000 or less) slowly at first, then faster, from about 80% at 7 to about 30% at 13 on the 1-16 scale.
